# WO-2026-08-07-31 — Cockpit /private-api origin boundary
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

> **🔴 WARWICK’S REQUIRED OUTCOME, verbatim, and it is the whole order:**
>
> *"The repair must answer Vex’s original governing question: **Can an untrusted webpage running in Warwick’s browser read from or perform actions against the Cockpit’s private upstream services through the proxy, without possessing an authority Warwick deliberately granted?** The accepted answer must become **NO**."*
>
> *"**Do not treat removal of reflected CORS headers alone as sufficient**: Vex has established that a browser write capable of avoiding preflight must also be prevented. Let the existing team choose the **smallest correct implementation** and **prove the actual browser-origin property**."*

**The implementation is YOURS to choose.** What follows is the property that must hold and the evidence that must exist — not a prescription. *(Larry has now twice prescribed a method that would have holed one of his own controls; he is not doing it a third time.)*

**AC1 — cross-origin READ refused.** `GET /private-api/<path>` with `Origin: https://evil.example` → **403**, **no forward to the upstream**, and **no `access-control-allow-origin` header emitted at all**. Prove the non-forward with a fake upstream that records every request it receives.

**AC2 — the Cockpit stops answering preflights on the upstream’s behalf.** An `OPTIONS` from a disallowed origin must not receive a blanket `204` advertising `allow-methods` the upstream never agreed to.

**AC3 — THE WRITE PATH. This is the AC that separates a real fix from a cosmetic one.** A **`text/plain` POST** — the case browsers **never** preflight — from a disallowed origin must be **refused before its body reaches the upstream**. **Vex established that deleting the CORS reflection stops the READ but NOT the WRITE.** Your fake upstream must record **zero** bytes of that body. **If AC3 is not proven by execution, this order is not met, whatever else passes.**

**AC4 — the legitimate path still works.** Same-origin requests and the real PWA route continue to function. **A repair that breaks the CareerAIR overlay is not a repair** — Warwick ruled explicitly against expanding scope or degrading the Cockpit to close this.

**AC5 — non-vacuity by mutation.** Restore the old permissive behaviour **in memory** and show the gate goes **RED**; report the exact count. **A gate that stays green against the known exploit is worthless.**

**AC6 — the gate must be able to RUN.** Vex’s F6 is the durable lesson: `/private-api` is **the one live-facing handler never extracted from `server.mjs`**, and `server.mjs` imports `db.mjs`, which opens two production pools at module scope — **so no existing gate could execute this handler, which is why the defect survived.** `static.mjs`, `provenance.mjs`, `rotation-report.mjs` and `down-reason.mjs` were all extracted for exactly this reason. **If your gate cannot reach the handler without importing `db.mjs`, say so at READ-BACK rather than working around it** — the proven route is the synthetic-credentials pattern (a creds file pointing at dead port `59999`), which Larry and Vex have both used successfully.

## Inputs supplied

- **The findings, supplied here because the review is deliberately off-repo** (Warwick’s publication ruling): **F1 CRITICAL `server.mjs:399-402`** — the Cockpit echoes an arbitrary `Origin` back as `access-control-allow-origin`, so a cross-origin page reads private upstream bodies. **F2 CRITICAL `server.mjs:374-382`** — a blanket `OPTIONS` responder returns `204` advertising `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS` and echoing arbitrary request headers, **answering the preflight on the upstream’s behalf without asking it**. **F6 INFO** — see AC6.
- **Vex’s own smallest correction, for reference and not as an instruction:** (a) delete the reflection; (b) delete the blanket OPTIONS; **(c) a positive `Origin` check returning 403 before forwarding — the load-bearing one, because (a)+(b) stop the read and NOT the write.** ~10 lines.
- **Proven GREEN and NOT to be disturbed:** opt-in gating (`COCKPIT_PRIVATE_API` unset → 404 with zero CORS headers), credential stripping (no cookies, no auth headers forwarded), SSRF containment, `redirect: 'manual'` with `location` not forwarded, the 40MB cap and 30s timeout. **Do not regress any of these while fixing the origin check.**
- `services/cockpit/clone-portability-check.mjs` @ `5b1409f` and `render-vm-check.mjs` @ `a00e3a3` — the house shape for a gate with a verdict layer, a vacuity guard and permanent in-memory mutation cases.
